branches.en: a packet of cigarettes left unopened
branches.cn: 一包没拆封的香烟

branches.en: a key handed back at a front desk
branches.cn: 在前台交还的一把钥匙

branches.en: a hall emptying before midnight
branches.cn: 午夜前空下来的大厅

branches.en: a screen returning to the desktop
branches.cn: 回到桌面的屏幕

branches.en: the same release applied to a habit and to a job
branches.cn: 同一种解脱，一次用于习惯，一次用于工作

intro.en: The word comes from the Latin noun for rest and a French verb of release, with English endings that build agents and related verbs.
intro.cn: 这个词来自拉丁语表示休息的名词与法语表示释放的动词，并加上构成施动者与相关动词的英语词尾。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root quiet- is shared with quiet, though the two English words have parted ways in meaning.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根 quiet- 与 quiet 共用，但这两个英语词在意义上已经分家。

items.meaning: a formal release of a right

definition_zh: 相当；颇；完全；十分；的确
definition_en: to a fairly large degree; completely or entirely; used to agree strongly with what has just been said
core_image: 一杯水被倒到杯口，刚好齐平而不溢出
scene: 看完演出，两人站在剧院门口争论这出戏到底好不好，谁也没有立刻走开。The play was quite good, but the ending felt rushed.
sceneCN: 这里 quite 是「相当、颇」（第 1 个义项：达到较大的程度但未到极致）；句意为这出戏相当不错，只是结尾显得仓促。画面里可留意：剧院门口的灯箱、还没散去的人群。

pos.zh: 相当；颇；完全；十分；的确

derivatives.zh: 与 quite 同源的形容词，用于 call it quits，指两清、扯平
同源动词，指停止或离开
re- 加同源词，指回报或报复

senses.title: To a fairly large degree
senses.definition: to a degree that is large but not extreme
senses.definitionCN: 达到较大但并未到极点的程度
senses.example: The film was quite good, though not great.
senses.exampleCN: 这部电影相当不错，虽然算不上出色。
senses.why: The oldest sense was completely or free of qualification, and English softened it into a strong but not absolute degree.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的意思是「完全、毫无保留」，英语把它弱化为一种强而不绝对的程度。

senses.title: Completely or entirely
senses.definition: entirely, with no reservation, especially in British speech
senses.definitionCN: 完全地、毫无保留地，尤见于英式口语
senses.example: I quite agree with you on that point.
senses.exampleCN: 在这一点上我完全同意你。
senses.why: The word began as a legal term for being clear of a debt or a claim, and being clear of any doubt produced the sense of entirely.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初是法律用语，指债务或主张已经清结；既然任何疑问都清除了，就生出「完全」这一层意思。

senses.title: Used to agree strongly
senses.definition: used alone or with a short reply to show strong agreement
senses.definitionCN: 单独使用或作简短回答，表示强烈的同意
senses.example: 'It is cold tonight.' 'Quite.'
senses.exampleCN: 「今晚真冷。」「的确。」
senses.why: If something is quite so, it is entirely so; a bare quite therefore affirms the previous statement without adding anything.
senses.whyCN: 如果某事 quite 如此，就是完全如此；单独一个 quite 因此是在肯定前一句话，不再另加内容。

intro.en: Quite comes from the same Latin root as quiet and quit, through a French word meaning cleared or free; from free of doubt came the sense of completely.
intro.cn: quite 与 quiet、quit 同出一个拉丁词根，经一个意为「清结、自由」的法语词传来；从「无疑」生出了「完全」的意思。

items.en: Quies meant rest, and the related adjective described a person or thing at rest and free from obligation.
items.cn: quies 意为休息，相关形容词形容处于安歇、免于义务的人或物。

items.en: Quietus was used in law for being cleared of a debt or a claim, that is, free and settled.
items.cn: quietus 在法律中用于表示债务或主张已清结，也就是自由、了结。

items.en: Old French quite carried the legal sense of cleared and free, and also the sense of entirely.
items.cn: 古法语 quite 既带有「清结、自由」的法律义，也带有「完全」义。

items.en: Middle English quite meant completely or without reservation, often in phrases of agreement.
items.cn: 中古英语的 quite 意为完全、毫无保留，常用于表示同意的说法。

items.en: Modern English weakened the word in everyday use to a fairly large degree, while keeping the older strong sense in British speech.
items.cn: 现代英语在日常用法中把它弱化为「相当」，而在英式口语里保留了较强的旧义。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the same root's English forms; the near-meaning group gathers adverbs of degree and agreement.
note.cn: 形近组收同词根的英语形式；近义组收表示程度与同意的副词。

entries.definition: Silent and calm.
entries.definitionCN: 安静而平静的。

entries.definition: To stop or leave.
entries.definitionCN: 停止或离开。

entries.definition: Even in a debt or a dispute, as in call it quits.
entries.definitionCN: 债务或争执两清，如 call it quits。

entries.definition: A literary word for calmness.
entries.definitionCN: 书面语，指宁静。

entries.definition: To a moderate degree.
entries.definitionCN: 达到中等程度地。

entries.definition: To a noticeable degree, often with a mild tone.
entries.definitionCN: 达到明显程度地，常带轻微语气。

entries.definition: In every way, entirely.
entries.definitionCN: 在各方面、完全地。

entries.definition: In precise agreement with something.
entries.definitionCN: 与某事物完全吻合地。

normalIntro.en: The word began as cleared and free, moved to entirely, and softened to fairly in everyday speech.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词从「清结、自由」开始，走到「完全」，又在日常口语里弱化为「相当」。

normal.en: Quite, quiet and quit all come from the Latin word for rest; only quite kept the legal sense of settled.
normal.cn: quite、quiet 与 quit 都出自拉丁语「休息」一词，只有 quite 保留了「了结」的法律义。

normal.en: Quite a few means a fairly large number, even though few alone suggests a small one.
normal.cn: quite a few 意为相当多，尽管 few 单独用时表示很少。

normal.en: Not quite is the polite way of saying almost, but not completely.
normal.cn: not quite 是「几乎但不完全」的客气说法。

normal.en: In British speech quite can mean entirely, while in American speech it more often means fairly.
normal.cn: 在英式口语里 quite 可指完全，在美式口语里更常指相当。

normal.en: A single quite in reply means you agree completely with the previous sentence.
normal.cn: 单独一个 quite 作回答，表示你完全同意上一句话。

abstract.en: A word that once meant free of every claim now measures how much of a claim is true.
abstract.cn: 一个曾表示「免除一切主张」的词，如今用来衡量一项主张有多少成真。

abstract.en: Quite is a word of proportion, and proportion is always judged by the ear rather than by the ruler.
abstract.cn: quite 是一个讲分寸的词，而分寸总是由耳朵来判断，而不是由尺子。

abstract.en: The strength of quite depends on the listener, which is why the same sentence can sound like praise or like faint damning.
abstract.cn: quite 的分量取决于听者，所以同一句话既能听起来像称赞，也能像淡淡的贬低。

examples.en: The room is quite small, but it is enough for one person.
examples.cn: 房间相当小，但一个人住够了。

examples.en: Are you quite sure you left the keys here?
examples.cn: 你十分确定把钥匙落在这里了吗？

examples.en: There were quite a few people waiting outside.
examples.cn: 外面等着的人相当多。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「快特」——比「快」还要特别一点，程度相当高，记住 quite 是相当、完全。

root: 拉丁语 quies（休息）→ quietus（清结、免除）→ 古法语 quite → 英语 quite；同族有 quiet、quit、quits、requite。

sensesIntro.en: The core is being clear and complete; the senses divide into a strong degree, full completeness and bare agreement.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「清结而完整」；义项分为较强程度、完全的完整性，以及单独表示同意。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a glass filled to the brim, level but not spilling.
core.cn: 核心意象：一杯水倒到杯口，齐平而不外溢。

branches.en: a film that is better than expected
branches.cn: 比预想更好的电影

branches.en: a debt marked paid in full
branches.cn: 标着「全部付清」的债务

branches.en: a single word of agreement in a quiet room
branches.cn: 安静房间里一个表示同意的单词

branches.en: the same word measuring a degree and closing a discussion
branches.cn: 同一个词既衡量程度，也结束讨论

branches.en: the legal fullness softened into everyday emphasis
branches.cn: 法律的「完全」被软化成日常的强调

intro.en: The word is a French borrowing on the Latin root of rest, and its English relatives are few but old.
intro.cn: 这个词是建立在拉丁语「休息」词根上的法语借词，它的英语亲属不多但很古老。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root quiet- also produced quiet and quit, though English split the meanings apart.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根 quiet- 也产生了 quiet 与 quit，只是英语把词义拆开了。

definition_zh: 小测验；知识问答；盘问
definition_en: a short test of knowledge; a game in which people answer questions; to ask a person a series of questions
core_image: 一叠翻到背面等着写答案的小纸片
scene: 教室里，老师把一叠小纸片发下来，大家翻到背面开始写答案。We had a short quiz on irregular verbs before the lesson began.
sceneCN: 这里 quiz 是「小测验」（第 1 个义项：检查知识的简短测试）；句意为正式上课前我们先做了一次不规则动词的小测验。画面里可留意：发下来的纸片、翻面的动作、还没开始的课本。

pos.zh: 小测验；知识问答；智力竞赛
盘问；考问

derivatives.zh: quiz 加 -er，指参加问答或喜欢做小测的人
与 quiz 同族，指带着疑问、略带打趣的表情
quizzical 加 -ly，指带着疑问神情地

senses.title: A short test of knowledge
senses.definition: a brief test given to check what someone has learned
senses.definitionCN: 为检查学习情况而进行的简短测试
senses.example: We had a quiz on irregular verbs this morning.
senses.exampleCN: 我们今天早上做了一次不规则动词的小测。
senses.why: The word entered American English as a term for an odd person or a bit of fun, and the test sense grew from playful questioning.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初以美式英语俚语身份出现，指古怪的人或一场玩笑，而「测验」义从这种嬉戏式的发问生长出来。

senses.title: A question-and-answer game
senses.definition: a game or show in which people compete by answering questions
senses.definitionCN: 人们通过回答问题来竞争的游戏或节目
senses.example: She won the pub quiz with her team.
senses.exampleCN: 她和队友一起赢了酒吧问答比赛。
senses.why: A quiz as a form of entertainment keeps the older playful tone: questions are asked for fun, not for a grade.
senses.whyCN: 作为娱乐形式的 quiz 保留了较早的嬉戏语气：提问是为了好玩，而不是为了打分。

senses.title: To ask someone many questions
senses.definition: to put a series of questions to a person, often to test or press them
senses.definitionCN: 向某人连续发问，常常是为了检验或施压
senses.example: The reporter quizzed the minister about the new tax.
senses.exampleCN: 记者就新税向部长连续发问。
senses.why: The verb reverses the direction of the noun: instead of answering questions, the subject is the one who fires them.
senses.whyCN: 动词把名词的方向颠倒过来：主语不再是回答问题的学生，而是连续抛出问题的人。

intro.en: Quiz is a word of uncertain origin that appeared in English only in the late eighteenth century, probably as slang; no reliable Latin source can be given.
intro.cn: quiz 来源不确定，直到十八世纪后期才在英语中出现，很可能是俚语；无法给出可靠的拉丁语来源。

items.en: The first records of quiz come from late eighteenth-century English, and dictionaries disagree about which slang use came first.
items.cn: quiz 的最早记录出现在十八世纪后期的英语中，各家词典对哪一种俚语用法在先并不一致。

items.en: The word was first used for an odd or eccentric person, and also for a joke or a piece of mockery.
items.cn: 这个词最初用来指古怪的人，也用来指玩笑或嘲弄。

items.en: In the nineteenth century quiz settled into the sense of a set of questions used to test knowledge.
items.cn: 到十九世纪，quiz 固定为「用来考查知识的一组问题」这一义项。

items.en: Schools made the quiz a short test, while radio and later television made it a popular question game.
items.cn: 学校把 quiz 做成简短测验，电台以及后来的电视又把它做成大众问答游戏。

items.en: Modern English uses quiz for a short test, for a quiz show and for the act of questioning someone closely.
items.cn: 现代英语用 quiz 指小测、问答节目以及紧追不舍地提问这一行为。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms built from the same short word; the near-meaning group gathers words for tests and questioning.
note.cn: 形近组收由这个短词构成的形式；近义组收表示测验与提问的词。

entries.definition: More than one short test.
entries.definitionCN: 不止一次小测验。

entries.definition: A person who takes part in quizzes.
entries.definitionCN: 参加问答的人。

entries.definition: Showing mild doubt or amusement.
entries.definitionCN: 带着轻微怀疑或打趣的。

entries.definition: The act of asking a series of questions.
entries.definitionCN: 连续发问的行为。

entries.definition: A set of questions used to measure knowledge.
entries.definitionCN: 用来衡量知识的一组问题。

entries.definition: A longer, formal test.
entries.definitionCN: 更长、更正式的考试。

entries.definition: A sentence that asks for information.
entries.definitionCN: 索取信息的问句。

entries.definition: To question someone thoroughly and formally.
entries.definitionCN: 彻底而正式地审问某人。

normalIntro.en: The word came from slang for a joke or an odd person, and the playful questioning at its heart became the school quiz and the quiz show.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词源自表示玩笑或怪人的俚语，其核心的嬉戏式发问后来变成学校小测与问答节目。

normal.en: Quiz, quizzes, quizzed: the doubled z is kept so the vowel stays short, as in a quiz but two quizzes.
normal.cn: quiz、quizzes、quizzed：双写 z 是为了保持短元音，所以一个 quiz，两个 quizzes。

normal.en: A pop quiz is one you did not prepare for, which is exactly why it is called pop.
normal.cn: a pop quiz 指你没准备的突击测验，正如 pop 一词所暗示的突然。

normal.en: Quiz show and quiz master name the television version of the same question game.
normal.cn: quiz show 与 quiz master 指同一个问答游戏的电视版本。

normal.en: To quiz a person is to ask question after question, as a reporter quizzes a minister.
normal.cn: to quiz 一个人就是接连发问，就像记者追问部长那样。

normal.en: A quiz is usually short and informal, while an exam is long and formal.
normal.cn: quiz 通常短而不正式，而 exam 长而正式。

abstract.en: A quiz measures what can be recalled under pressure, not everything a person knows.
abstract.cn: 测验衡量的是压力下能回想起来的部分，而非一个人所知的全部。

abstract.en: The same word serves a classroom and a television studio because both turn knowledge into a game.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既用于教室也用于演播室，因为两者都把知识变成游戏。

abstract.en: Being quizzed is being asked to justify yourself in someone else's order of questions.
abstract.cn: 被盘问，就是被要求按别人设定的问题顺序为自己作解释。

examples.en: The teacher gave us a ten-minute quiz at the end of class.
examples.cn: 老师在课末给了我们一次十分钟的小测。

examples.en: Our team came second in the science quiz.
examples.cn: 我们队在科学问答比赛中得了第二。

examples.en: Reporters quizzed the coach about the sudden change of players.
examples.cn: 记者们就突然换人的事追问教练。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「窥子」——老师从小纸片里窥见你记住了多少，记住 quiz 是小测验。

root: 来源不确定，通常认为出自十八世纪后期英语俚语，先指怪人或玩笑，后转指一问一答的测验；没有可靠的拉丁语来源。

sensesIntro.en: The core is playful questioning; the senses divide into a short school test, a question game and the act of pressing someone with questions.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是嬉戏式的发问；义项分为学校小测、问答游戏，以及连续向某人施压提问的行为。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stack of small cards turned face down, waiting for answers.
core.cn: 核心意象：一叠翻到背面、等着写答案的小卡片。

branches.en: a card turned over on a desk
branches.cn: 桌上翻过来的一张卡片

branches.en: buzzers on a television stage
branches.cn: 电视舞台上的一排抢答器

branches.en: a reporter holding a recorder forward
branches.cn: 记者把录音笔伸向前方

branches.en: the same questions asked for a grade and for fun
branches.cn: 同样的问题，一次为分数，一次为乐趣

branches.en: questions that entertain an audience and questions that press a witness
branches.cn: 取悦观众的问题与向证人施压的问题

intro.en: The word is too recent to have a Latin structure; what it does have is a short English root and a set of endings and compounds built on it.
intro.cn: 这个词出现得太晚，没有拉丁语结构；它有的是一个简短的英语词根，以及在此基础上构成的词尾与复合词。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁语同族词记录。

definition_zh: 引语；引用；报价
definition_en: a group of words taken from a text or speech and repeated by someone else; the act of repeating such words; a price stated for goods or work
core_image: 一段被原样抄进新纸页的旧句子，句尾标着出处
scene: 论文的第一页上，作者把一段旧演讲原样抄下，并在句后标明出处。The first page of the essay carries a quotation from an old speech.
sceneCN: 这里 quotation 是「引语」（第 1 个义项：从别处摘来并逐字重复的一段话）；句意为论文第一页引用了那段旧演讲中的一句话。画面里可留意：第一页、抄下的句子、句后的出处。

pos.zh: 引语；引用；报价

derivatives.zh: quotation 的动词原形，指引用或报价
quote 加 -able，指值得引用的
quotable 加 -ity，指值得被引用的程度

senses.title: Words taken from another source
senses.definition: a passage repeated word for word from a book, speech or document
senses.definitionCN: 从书、演讲或文件中逐字重复的一段话
senses.example: The essay opens with a quotation from an old speech.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇文章以一段旧演讲的引语开头。
senses.why: Medieval Latin quotare meant to mark a text by numbers so passages could be cited, and the passage so marked became the quotation.
senses.whyCN: 中世纪拉丁语 quotare 意为给文本标号以便引证，被这样标出的一段话就成了 quotation。

senses.title: The act of repeating words
senses.definition: the act of repeating someone else's words, with or without credit
senses.definitionCN: 重复他人话语的行为，无论是否注明出处
senses.example: Quotation without credit is a form of theft.
senses.exampleCN: 不加注明地引用是一种剽窃。
senses.why: Once the noun named the copied passage, it also named the act of copying it, and the moral question of credit followed.
senses.whyCN: 名词既指抄下来的段落，也指抄写这一行为，随之而来的是「是否注明出处」的伦理问题。

senses.title: A stated price
senses.definition: a price given in advance for goods or for a piece of work
senses.definitionCN: 为货物或某项工作预先给出的价格
senses.example: Ask the builder for a quotation before you agree.
senses.exampleCN: 答应之前先向施工方要一份报价。
senses.why: A trader who quotes a price marks it out in advance, and the same Latin verb of marking produced this commercial sense.
senses.whyCN: 商人报出价格，就是把价格预先标定出来；同一个表示「标记」的拉丁语动词也生出了这层商业义。

intro.en: Quotation comes from a medieval Latin verb meaning to mark a book by numbers, built on the Latin word for how many, and reached English through French.
intro.cn: quotation 源自一个意为「给书编号」的中世纪拉丁语动词，其基础是拉丁语表示「多少」的词，并经法语进入英语。

items.en: Quot was the Latin word for how many, used in phrases that numbered chapters and lines.
items.cn: quot 是拉丁语表示「多少」的词，用于给章节与诗行编号的说法。

items.en: Quotare meant to number the chapters of a book so that a passage could be pointed to precisely.
items.cn: quotare 意为给书的章节编号，以便精确指出某一段落。

items.en: The derived noun named the act of numbering, and by extension the passage marked with a number.
items.cn: 由其构成的名词指编号这一行为，并引申指标上了号码的那段文字。

items.en: French carried the noun into English, where it came to mean the repeated passage itself.
items.cn: 法语把这个名词带入英语，在英语里它转指被重复的那段文字本身。

items.en: Modern English uses quotation for cited words, for the act of citing them, and for a price stated in advance.
items.cn: 现代英语用 quotation 指被引用的话、引用这一行为，以及预先报出的价格。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms on the Latin stem of numbering; the near-meaning group gathers words for cited passages and prices.
note.cn: 形近组收拉丁语「编号」词干上的形式；近义组收表示被引段落与价格的词。

entries.definition: To repeat words or to state a price.
entries.definitionCN: 重复他人的话，或报出价格。

entries.definition: Worth being repeated in another text.
entries.definitionCN: 值得被别的文本引用的。

entries.definition: A fixed share of something allowed to a group.
entries.definitionCN: 分配给某群体的固定份额。

entries.definition: The result of dividing one number by another.
entries.definitionCN: 一个数除以另一个数所得的结果。

entries.definition: A reference to a source, or words taken from it.
entries.definitionCN: 对来源的引用，或从来源中摘出的话。

entries.definition: A short passage taken from a longer work.
entries.definitionCN: 从较长作品中摘出的短段。

entries.definition: An approximate price or amount given in advance.
entries.definitionCN: 预先给出的约略价格或数量。

entries.definition: The amount of money asked for something.
entries.definitionCN: 为某物索要的金额。

normalIntro.en: The word began as numbering a text so a passage could be found, and the marked passage became the quotation we cite today.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词从「给文本编号以便找到某段」开始，被标出的段落就成了今天我们引用的 quotation。

normal.en: Quotation and quote share the Latin question how many, because early citations were marked with chapter numbers.
normal.cn: quotation 与 quote 共用拉丁语「多少」这一问，因为早期的引证靠章节编号来标记。

normal.en: Quotation marks are the written signs that enclose the borrowed words.
normal.cn: quotation marks 是围住借来之话的书写符号。

normal.en: A direct quotation repeats the exact words, while an indirect one reports their meaning without quotation marks.
normal.cn: 直接引语逐字重复原话，间接引语只转述意思而不用引号。

normal.en: A price quotation is the builder's way of quoting a figure before the work starts.
normal.cn: 报价（price quotation）是施工方在工作开始前报出数字的方式。

normal.en: Quotable means good enough to be repeated by other people.
normal.cn: quotable 意为好到值得被别人重复引用。

abstract.en: To quote is to let another voice speak inside your own sentence, and quotation marks mark the boundary of that borrowed voice.
abstract.cn: 引用就是让另一个声音在你的句子里说话，引号标出了这个借来之音的边界。

abstract.en: Every quotation is a small act of trust: the reader trusts that the words were really said or written.
abstract.cn: 每一次引用都是一次小小的信任行为：读者相信这些话确实被说过或写过。

abstract.en: The same word names a cited sentence and a price, because both are figures marked out in advance for others to accept.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既指被引用的一句话，也指一个价格，因为两者都是预先标出、等待别人接受的数字。

examples.en: The report begins with a quotation from the mayor's speech.
examples.cn: 报告以市长演讲中的一段引语开头。

examples.en: Put the quotation in quotation marks and add the page number.
examples.cn: 把这段引语放进引号里，并补上页码。

examples.en: We accepted the quotation for the roof repair.
examples.cn: 我们接受了屋顶维修的报价。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「阔贴身」——把别人的好句子阔气地贴在自己文章里，记得标出处，记住 quotation 是引语。

root: 拉丁语 quot（多少）→ 中世纪拉丁语 quotare（给章节编号）→ quotationem → 法语 quotation → 英语 quotation；同族有 quote、quota、quotient。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a marked passage; the senses divide into the cited words, the act of citing them and a price marked out in advance.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「被标出的段落」；义项分为被引用的文字、引用这一行为，以及预先标出的价格。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an old sentence copied onto a fresh page, its source noted at the end.
core.cn: 核心意象：一段旧句子被抄到新纸上，句末标着出处。

branches.en: a sentence in quotation marks
branches.cn: 放在引号里的一句话

branches.en: a pen copying a line by hand
branches.cn: 用手逐字抄下一行

branches.en: a figure written on a builder's letter
branches.cn: 写在施工方信函上的一个数字

branches.en: the borrowed words and the act of borrowing them
branches.cn: 借来的话与借这一动作

branches.en: the same marking done to a text and to a price
branches.cn: 同一种标记，一次标在文本上，一次标在价格上

intro.en: The word is built from the Latin question of how many, a verb of numbering, its noun of action and the French form that reached English.
intro.cn: 这个词由拉丁语「多少」这一问、表示编号的动词、其动作名词，以及进入英语的法语形式构成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family around quot is small but productive in English.
latinIntro.cn: 围绕 quot 的拉丁词群不大，却在英语里颇有生产力。

definition_zh: 引用；引述；报价；引语；报价单
definition_en: to repeat words from a text or speaker; to state a price for goods or work; words repeated from a source; a stated price
core_image: 录音笔倒回到开头，屏幕上是逐字对照的文稿
scene: 记者把录音倒回开头，逐字核对手稿里引用的那句话。The reporter checked the words she planned to quote from the interview.
sceneCN: 这里 quote 是「引用、引述」（第 1 个义项：重复别人说过或写过的话）；句意为记者核对了她准备从采访中引用的那段话。画面里可留意：倒回的录音、逐字的文稿、圈出的句子。

pos.zh: 引用；引述；报价
引语；报价单；引号（口语）

collocations.zh: 所谓（口语，表示照搬别人的说法）

derivatives.zh: quote 加 -ation，指引语、引用行为或报价
quote 加 -able，指值得引用的
mis- 加 quote，指错误地引用
un- 与 quote 相对，指结束引文，多用于 quote unquote 的口语说法

senses.title: To repeat another's words
senses.definition: to repeat the exact words that someone has said or written
senses.definitionCN: 逐字重复别人说过或写过的话
senses.example: She quoted a line from the report.
senses.exampleCN: 她引用了报告里的一句话。
senses.why: The Latin verb behind the word meant to mark a passage with a number, and later to read it out with a marker, which is what citation is.
senses.whyCN: 这个词背后的拉丁语动词本指给某段落标上编号，后来指标记着朗读，这正是引用的动作。

senses.title: To state a price
senses.definition: to tell a customer in advance how much goods or work will cost
senses.definitionCN: 事先告诉顾客货物或工作要花多少钱
senses.example: The garage quoted three hundred pounds for the repair.
senses.exampleCN: 修车行对这单维修报了三百英镑。
senses.why: A merchant who marks a price on goods is marking a figure for the buyer, the same marking verb used for texts.
senses.whyCN: 商人在货物上标价，就是为买家标出一个数字，与给文本标号用的是同一个动词。

senses.title: Words repeated from a source
senses.definition: a passage repeated from a book, speech or interview, used as a noun
senses.definitionCN: 从书、演讲或采访中取来重复的一段话，作名词用
senses.example: He put a quote from the coach on the wall.
senses.exampleCN: 他把教练的一句话贴在墙上。
senses.why: English speakers shortened quotation to quote, and the shorter form kept the meaning of the cited passage.
senses.whyCN: 英语使用者把 quotation 缩略为 quote，这个较短的形式保留了「被引段落」的意思。

senses.title: A stated price
senses.definition: a price given in writing or in speech before work begins, used as a noun
senses.definitionCN: 在工作开始前以书面或口头给出的价格，作名词用
senses.example: The quote came in higher than we expected.
senses.exampleCN: 报价比我们预想的高。
senses.why: The verb to quote a price produced a noun quote for the figure itself, common in building and insurance work.
senses.whyCN: 动词「报价」产生了名词 quote，指那个价格数字本身，在建筑与保险行业很常见。

intro.en: Quote is the shortened form of quotation, and both go back to a Latin verb of numbering and marking that came to English through French.
intro.cn: quote 是 quotation 的缩略形式，两者都可追溯到拉丁语中表示编号与标记的动词，并经法语进入英语。

items.en: Quot meant how many and appeared in the numbering of chapters and lines.
items.cn: quot 意为多少，出现在给章节与诗行编号的用法中。

items.en: Quotare meant to mark a book with numbers so that a passage could be found and cited.
items.cn: quotare 意为用数字标记书本，以便找到并引证某段。

items.en: Old French quoter kept the sense of marking and citing, and also of setting a price.
items.cn: 古法语 quoter 保留了标记与引证的意思，也指定价。

items.en: Middle English used quote for citing and for stating a price, two senses that still stand side by side.
items.cn: 中古英语的 quote 既指引证，也指定价，这两层意思至今并列。

items.en: Modern English shortened quotation to quote, especially in speech, journalism and trade.
items.cn: 现代英语把 quotation 缩略为 quote，尤其在口语、新闻与商贸中。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms on the Latin stem of numbering; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of citing, repeating and pricing.
note.cn: 形近组收拉丁语「编号」词干上的形式；近义组收表示引用、重复与定价的动词。

entries.definition: Cited words, or a price given in advance.
entries.definitionCN: 被引用的话，或预先给出的价格。

entries.definition: Worth repeating in another text.
entries.definitionCN: 值得在别的文本中重复的。

entries.definition: A fixed share assigned to a group.
entries.definitionCN: 分配给一个群体的固定份额。

entries.definition: The number produced by division.
entries.definitionCN: 除法所得的数。

entries.definition: To mention a source formally, especially in writing.
entries.definitionCN: 正式提到一个来源，尤指在写作中。

entries.definition: To say or do something again.
entries.definitionCN: 再说或再做一遍。

entries.definition: To give an approximate figure in advance.
entries.definitionCN: 预先给出约略数字。

entries.definition: To set the amount of money asked for something.
entries.definitionCN: 确定某物索要的金额。

normalIntro.en: The word marks a passage or a price: both are figures set out for others to read, repeat or accept.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词标记一段话或一个价格：两者都是摆出来供别人阅读、重复或接受的数字。

normal.en: Quote is a shortened quotation, so the noun and the verb look exactly alike.
normal.cn: quote 是 quotation 的缩略，所以名词和动词长得一模一样。

normal.en: Quote unquote is the spoken way of putting quotation marks around someone else's phrase.
normal.cn: quote unquote 是口语中给别人的说法加上引号的方式。

normal.en: A builder's quote is a price marked on paper, using the same verb as quoting a sentence.
normal.cn: 施工方的 quote 是写在纸上的价格，用的动词与引用一句话相同。

normal.en: To quote someone on a subject is to report their exact words about it.
normal.cn: quote someone on 某话题，就是报告他们对这个话题的原话。

normal.en: Misquote means to get the words wrong, and it is one of the commonest complaints in journalism.
normal.cn: misquote 意为引错话，是新闻业最常见的投诉之一。

abstract.en: To quote well is to disappear for a moment and let the other voice be heard clearly.
abstract.cn: 引得好，就是让自己暂时消失，让另一个声音被清楚地听见。

abstract.en: A price quoted in advance is a promise about the future, which is why a quote can feel like a commitment.
abstract.cn: 预先报出的价格是对未来的一个承诺，所以 quote 会让人觉得像一种约定。

abstract.en: Quoting and pricing both fix a number in place, one on a page and one on a market.
abstract.cn: 引用与定价都是把一个数字固定下来，一个固定在纸页上，一个固定在市场上。

examples.en: She quoted the contract exactly in her letter.
examples.cn: 她在信里一字不差地引用了合同。

examples.en: The shop quoted me a lower price for the same chair.
examples.cn: 同一把椅子，这家店给我报的价更低。

examples.en: He wrote the coach's quote on a card above his desk.
examples.cn: 他把教练的那句话写在一张卡片上，贴到书桌上方。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「阔特」——阔气地把别人的话原样搬来，记得标出处，记住 quote 是引用。

root: 拉丁语 quot（多少）→ 中世纪拉丁语 quotare（编号、标记）→ 古法语 quoter → 英语 quote；同族有 quotation、quota、quotient。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a marked figure; the senses divide into repeating words, setting a price, the repeated words themselves and the price itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「被标出的数字或段落」；义项分为重复他人的话、定出价格、被重复的话本身，以及价格本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a recorder wound back to the start, beside a word-for-word transcript.
core.cn: 核心意象：倒回开头的录音笔，旁边放着逐字对照的文稿。

branches.en: a finger tracing one line twice
branches.cn: 手指把一行字描了两遍

branches.en: a figure written on an order form
branches.cn: 写在订单上的一个数字

branches.en: a sentence framed on a wall
branches.cn: 被框起来挂在墙上的一句话

branches.en: a sum circled at the bottom of a letter
branches.cn: 信末被圈出的金额

branches.en: the act of quoting and the thing quoted
branches.cn: 引用的动作与被引用之物

intro.en: The word is a shortened French borrowing on the Latin root of numbering, with English endings that build nouns, adjectives and negative verbs.
intro.cn: 这个词是建立在拉丁语「编号」词根上的法语缩略借词，加上构成名词、形容词与否定动词的英语词尾。

latinIntro.en: The stem quot- also gave quota and quotient, which keep the plain idea of a counted share.
latinIntro.cn: quot- 这个词干还给出了 quota 与 quotient，它们保留了「被计算出的份额」这一朴素意思。

definition_zh: 赛跑；竞赛；种族；急奔；（磨坊）水道
definition_en: a competition to see who is fastest; a contest between people or groups; a group of people sharing ancestry; to move very fast; a channel of water leading to a mill
core_image: 傍晚的跑道上，几名选手同时冲过起跑线
scene: 傍晚的跑道上，发令枪响后几名选手同时冲出起跑线。He won the final race by less than a second.
sceneCN: 这里 race 是「赛跑、竞速比赛」（第 1 个义项：比谁跑得快的比赛）；句意为他以不到一秒的优势赢下了最后一场比赛。画面里可留意：起点线、发令枪、几乎并排的身影。

pos.zh: 赛跑；竞赛；种族；（磨坊）水道
急速行进；参赛；使拼命跑

derivatives.zh: race 加 -er，指参赛者或赛车
race 加 -ing，指赛跑、赛车等竞技活动
race 加 -ial，指与种族有关的
race 加 -ist，指持种族歧视观点的

senses.title: A competition of speed
senses.definition: a contest to find who or what is fastest
senses.definitionCN: 比出谁或什么最快的一种竞赛
senses.example: He won the hundred-metre race.
senses.exampleCN: 他赢下了百米赛跑。
senses.why: The contest sense comes from an old northern word for a rush or a run, so the word began as the movement itself.
senses.whyCN: 比赛义来自一个古老的北方词，意为「急冲、奔跑」，所以这个词最初指的就是那股奔跑。

senses.title: A contest between people or groups
senses.definition: a situation in which people or groups try to be first to reach a goal
senses.definitionCN: 人或群体争相抢先达到某个目标的情形
senses.example: The race for the contract ended in a tie.
senses.exampleCN: 争取这份合同的竞争以平局收场。
senses.why: Once a race was a run toward a line, any struggle to arrive first could be called a race, even without running.
senses.whyCN: 当 race 指朝终点线奔跑之后，任何「抢在前头」的争夺都可以叫 race，即使根本不用跑。

senses.title: A group sharing ancestry
senses.definition: a group of people regarded as sharing ancestry and physical features, a term used with care
senses.definitionCN: 被视为共享血统与外貌特征的一群人，此词使用时须谨慎
senses.example: People of every race took part in the survey.
senses.exampleCN: 各种族的人都参加了这项调查。
senses.why: This sense comes from a different source, an Italian word for kind or breed, and its scientific status has been much debated.
senses.whyCN: 这一义项来源不同，出自一个意为「种类、品种」的意大利语词，其科学地位一直备受争议。

senses.title: To move very fast
senses.definition: to move at great speed, often in a hurry or in competition
senses.definitionCN: 以很快的速度移动，常带匆忙或竞争意味
senses.example: She raced to catch the last bus.
senses.exampleCN: 她飞奔去赶末班车。
senses.why: Since the word first named a rush, the verb simply describes the act of rushing, with or without a contest.
senses.whyCN: 既然这个词最初指一股急冲，动词就只是描述急冲这一动作，无论有没有比赛。

senses.title: A channel of water
senses.definition: a fast current of water, especially one made to drive a mill wheel
senses.definitionCN: 流速较快的水道，尤指为驱动磨坊水轮而开的渠道
senses.example: The old mill still stands beside the race.
senses.exampleCN: 那座老磨坊仍然立在水道旁边。
senses.why: Water rushing through a narrow channel moves like a runner, so the old sense of a rush survived in the mill race.
senses.whyCN: 水冲过窄渠时像奔跑者一样急行，于是「急冲」这一古老意思在磨坊水道里保留下来。

intro.en: Race is really two words: the contest sense comes from an old northern word for a rush, while the ancestry sense comes through French and Italian from a word of uncertain origin.
intro.cn: race 实际上是两个词：比赛义来自古老的北方词「急冲」，而种族义经法语与意大利语来自一个来源不确定的词。

items.en: Ras meant a running or a rush, and it entered northern English with the sense of swift movement.
items.cn: ras 意为奔跑、急冲，带着快速运动的意思进入英格兰北部英语。

items.en: Middle English race named a run or a course, and from that a contest of speed.
items.cn: 中古英语的 race 指一次奔跑或一段跑道，由此生出速度竞赛之义。

items.en: A separate French word razza, of uncertain origin, meant a breed or a kind, especially of animals.
items.cn: 另一个来源不确定的法语词 razza 意为品种或种类，尤指动物的品种。

items.en: English applied the breed sense to groups of people, a use that later became scientifically and socially disputed.
items.cn: 英语把「品种」义用到人群上，这一用法后来在科学与社会层面都引发争议。

items.en: Modern English keeps both words: race as a contest and race as a category of people, plus the mill race of flowing water.
items.cn: 现代英语保留了两个词：作为竞赛的 race、作为人群类别的 race，以及指流水渠道的磨坊 race。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms built on the word; the near-meaning group gathers words for contests, speed and ancestry.
note.cn: 形近组收由这个词构成的形式；近义组收表示竞赛、速度与血统的词。

entries.definition: A person or vehicle that takes part in races.
entries.definitionCN: 参加比赛的人或车辆。

entries.definition: The sport of competing for speed.
entries.definitionCN: 比速度的竞技运动。

entries.definition: Connected with a group sharing ancestry.
entries.definitionCN: 与共享血统的群体有关的。

entries.definition: Someone who treats people unequally because of their group.
entries.definitionCN: 因所属群体而区别对待他人的人。

entries.definition: A competition in which people try to win.
entries.definitionCN: 人们争胜的比赛。

entries.definition: The activity of trying to do better than others.
entries.definitionCN: 力图胜过他人的活动。

entries.definition: To run at top speed for a short distance.
entries.definitionCN: 短距离全速奔跑。

entries.definition: Belonging to a group with shared culture and origin.
entries.definitionCN: 属于共享文化与来源的群体。

normalIntro.en: The contest sense grew from a word for a rush of movement, and the ancestry sense grew from a word for breed; English keeps both under one spelling.
normalIntro.cn: 比赛义从表示「急冲」的词生长出来，种族义从表示「品种」的词生长出来；英语把两者放在同一个拼写之下。

normal.en: Race as a contest and race as a category of people have different origins that happen to share one spelling.
normal.cn: 作为竞赛的 race 与作为人群类别的 race 来源不同，只是碰巧共用同一个拼写。

normal.en: A race against time is a race with no competitor but the clock.
normal.cn: race against time 是没有对手、只与时钟赛跑的比赛。

normal.en: Racer, racing and racial all come from the same short word with different endings.
normal.cn: racer、racing、racial 都是同一个短词加上不同词尾。

normal.en: A mill race is water rushing through a channel, which shows how old the sense of a rush really is.
normal.cn: mill race 指冲过渠道的水，可见「急冲」这一古老意思有多深。

normal.en: The human race uses race in the broad sense of all people together, not in the sense of a category.
normal.cn: the human race 用的是「全人类」这一宽泛义，而不是「某一类别」义。

abstract.en: Sorting people into races says more about the sorter than about the people being sorted.
abstract.cn: 把人分成种族，更多说明分类者本身，而不是被分类的人。

abstract.en: A race is exciting because everyone agrees on the same finish line, which is also why disagreements about the line are so bitter.
abstract.cn: 比赛令人兴奋，因为大家认同同一条终点线，这也正是关于终点线的分歧如此激烈的原因。

abstract.en: Speed is easy to measure and easy to admire, which is why so much of modern life is arranged as a race.
abstract.cn: 速度容易测量，也容易赞美，所以现代生活有很大一部分被安排成一场比赛。

examples.en: She came second in the school race.
examples.cn: 她在学校赛跑中得了第二。

examples.en: The two companies are in a race to launch first.
examples.cn: 两家公司在争抢谁先发布。

examples.en: He raced down the stairs when he heard the alarm.
examples.cn: 听到警报，他飞奔下楼。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「锐丝」——像一根锐利的丝线划过终点，速度极快，记住 race 是赛跑、竞赛。

root: 比赛义源于古诺斯语 ras（奔跑、急冲）；种族义经法语与意大利语来自 razza（品种，来源不确定）；两词在英语中同形。同族有 racer、racing、racial。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a rush; one branch runs from rush to contest, the other from breed to ancestry, and a third survives in the channel of a mill.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「急冲」；一条支线从急冲走到竞赛，另一条从品种走到血统，还有一条留在磨坊的水道里。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: runners leaving the start line together on an evening track.
core.cn: 核心意象：傍晚跑道上同时冲出起跑线的选手。

branches.en: a gun fired beside a track
branches.cn: 跑道旁打响的发令枪

branches.en: two firms chasing one contract
branches.cn: 两家公司争抢同一份合同

branches.en: a form asking for ancestry
branches.cn: 要求填写血统的表格

branches.en: feet taking the stairs three at a time
branches.cn: 一步三级地冲下楼梯

branches.en: the same rush, once on legs and once in a mill channel
branches.cn: 同一种急冲，一次靠双腿，一次在磨坊渠道里

intro.en: The contest word is native and northern, the ancestry word came through French and Italian, and English adds its usual endings to both.
intro.cn: 表示竞赛的词是本族词，来自北方；表示血统的词经法语和意大利语传来；英语给两者加上了惯用的词尾。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin source is recorded for either word.
latinIntro.cn: 这两个来源都没有可靠的拉丁语出处记录。

definition_zh: 种族的；种族间的；按种族划分的
definition_en: connected with a group of people regarded as sharing ancestry; happening between such groups; based on grouping people in that way
core_image: 一张表格上并排列着几个用来勾选族群的方框
scene: 会议室里摊着一份调查报告，讨论的是不同族群在招聘中受到的待遇。The report called for an end to racial discrimination in hiring.
sceneCN: 这里 racial 是「种族的」（第 1 个义项：与按血统划分的人群有关的）；句意为这份报告呼吁终止招聘中的种族歧视。画面里可留意：摊开的报告、并排的勾选框、沉默的与会者。

pos.zh: 种族的；种族间的；按种族划分的

derivatives.zh: racial 的词根名词，指按血统划分的人群类别
race 加 -ism，指种族歧视与种族主义
race 加 -ist，指带种族歧视态度的
racial 加 -ly，指从种族角度、按种族地

senses.title: Connected with a group by ancestry
senses.definition: relating to a group of people who are regarded as sharing ancestry and physical features
senses.definitionCN: 与被视为共享血统与外貌特征的一群人有关的
senses.example: The law forbids racial discrimination in hiring.
senses.exampleCN: 法律禁止招聘中的种族歧视。
senses.why: The adjective simply adds a relating suffix to the noun race, and the noun itself came from a word for breed.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词只是在名词 race 后加了表示「相关」的后缀，而那个名词本身来自表示「品种」的词。

senses.title: Happening between such groups
senses.definition: existing or occurring between different groups of people
senses.definitionCN: 存在于不同人群之间或发生在他们之间的
senses.example: Racial tension rose sharply after the election.
senses.exampleCN: 选举之后，族群之间的紧张关系急剧上升。
senses.why: Once the adjective described a group, it could also describe what happens when two such groups meet.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词既能描述一个群体，也就能描述两个这样的群体相遇时发生的事。

senses.title: Based on grouping by ancestry
senses.definition: organized or collected according to categories of ancestry
senses.definitionCN: 按照血统类别来组织或收集的
senses.example: The census collects racial data alongside age and income.
senses.exampleCN: 人口普查在收集年龄与收入数据的同时，也收集种族数据。
senses.why: Bureaucracies count people in categories, and a category built on ancestry is described as racial.
senses.whyCN: 行政机构按类别清点人口，而以血统划分的类别就被形容为 racial。

intro.en: Racial is the noun race with the Latin-derived ending -ial; the noun itself came into English through French and Italian from a word of uncertain origin meaning breed.
intro.cn: racial 是名词 race 加上源自拉丁语的词尾 -ial；那个名词本身经法语和意大利语进入英语，来自一个来源不确定、意为「品种」的词。

items.en: Razza meant a breed or a kind, especially of animals, and its own origin is uncertain.
items.cn: razza 意为品种或种类，尤指动物的品种，它本身的来源也不确定。

items.en: French race carried the sense of breed and stock, and English borrowed it in the sixteenth century.
items.cn: 法语 race 带有「品种、血统」的意思，英语在十六世纪借入。

items.en: English race extended the breed sense to groups of people, a use that later became the subject of scientific debate.
items.cn: 英语的 race 把「品种」义扩展到人群，这一用法后来成为科学争论的对象。

items.en: The ending -ial, from Latin adjective endings, forms words meaning relating to.
items.cn: 词尾 -ial 来自拉丁语形容词词尾，构成意为「与……有关的」词。

items.en: Modern English uses racial for what concerns such groups and for what happens between them.
items.cn: 现代英语用 racial 指与此类群体有关的事，以及发生在它们之间的事。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms built on the noun; the near-meaning group gathers adjectives about peoples and cultures.
note.cn: 形近组收由该名词构成的形式；近义组收表示人群与文化的形容词。

entries.definition: A group regarded as sharing ancestry.
entries.definitionCN: 被视为共享血统的一群人。

entries.definition: Prejudice or unfair treatment based on a group.
entries.definitionCN: 基于所属群体的偏见或不公对待。

entries.definition: Showing prejudice against another group.
entries.definitionCN: 对另一群体表现出偏见的。

entries.definition: A person who competes for speed, from the other race.
entries.definitionCN: 参加竞速的人，来自另一个同形的 race。

entries.definition: Relating to a group with shared culture and origin.
entries.definitionCN: 与共享文化和来源的群体有关的。

entries.definition: Relating to a whole country or people.
entries.definitionCN: 与整个国家或民族有关的。

entries.definition: Relating to shared customs and arts.
entries.definitionCN: 与共同习俗和艺术有关的。

entries.definition: Relating to a tribe or tribes.
entries.definitionCN: 与部落有关的。

normalIntro.en: The word is simply race turned into an adjective, so it describes anything done or counted by categories of ancestry.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词就是 race 变来的形容词，因此描述任何按血统类别来做或来清点的事情。

normal.en: Racial is race plus -ial, and -ial is the ending that makes a noun into an adjective of relation.
normal.cn: racial 就是 race 加 -ial，而 -ial 正是把名词变成关系形容词的词尾。

normal.en: Racism is the belief or practice, racial is what relates to groups, and racist describes a person or act.
normal.cn: racism 是信念或做法，racial 指与群体相关的，racist 形容人或行为。

normal.en: Racially is the adverb, as in racially mixed schools.
normal.cn: racially 是副词，如 racially mixed schools（种族混合的学校）。

normal.en: Racial profiling names the practice of suspecting people because of their group.
normal.cn: racial profiling 指因所属群体而怀疑某人的做法。

normal.en: The word has no comparative form because it does not admit degrees.
normal.cn: 这个词没有比较级，因为它不表示程度。

abstract.en: A category becomes an adjective, and the adjective then shapes how people are seen before they are met.
abstract.cn: 一个类别变成了形容词，而这个形容词又在你见到人之前塑造了你如何看待他们。

abstract.en: Words like racial record a way of sorting, and sorting is never only descriptive.
abstract.cn: racial 这样的词记录了一种分类方式，而分类从来不只是描述性的。

abstract.en: Calling something racial can describe a fact and also issue a judgement, depending on the sentence around it.
abstract.cn: 把某事称作 racial，既可能在描述事实，也可能在作出判断，取决于它所在的句子。

examples.en: The school has a clear policy against racial abuse.
examples.cn: 这所学校有明确的规定反对种族侮辱。

examples.en: They collected racial data for the study.
examples.cn: 他们为这项研究收集了种族数据。

examples.en: Racial equality remains a goal rather than a fact in many places.
examples.cn: 在许多地方，种族平等仍是目标而非事实。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「锐秀」——把人群锐利地分门别类，正好提醒你 racial 是种族的。

root: 意大利语 razza（品种，来源不确定）→ 法语 race（品种、血统）→ 英语 race + -ial → racial；同族有 racism、racist、racially。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a category of ancestry; the senses divide into what belongs to one group, what happens between groups, and what is organized by such categories.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「按血统划分的类别」；义项分为属于某一群体的、发生在群体之间的，以及按这类类别组织的。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a form with several boxes for ancestry placed side by side.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张表格上并排放着的几个血统勾选框。

branches.en: a hiring form with a blank for group
branches.cn: 招聘表上一栏留给族群的空格

branches.en: two groups facing each other across a table
branches.cn: 隔着桌子相对的两个群体

branches.en: a census sheet filled in by hand
branches.cn: 手工填写的人口普查表

branches.en: the same category seen from inside and from between
branches.cn: 同一个类别，从内部看与从之间看

branches.en: tension between groups and the counting that records it
branches.cn: 群体间的紧张与记录它的清点

intro.en: The word is a borrowed noun of breed plus a Latin-derived relating suffix, with English endings that build the abstract noun and the adverb.
intro.cn: 这个词是借来的「品种」名词加上源自拉丁语的关系后缀，再加上构成抽象名词与副词的英语词尾。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin source is recorded for the noun race itself.
latinIntro.cn: 名词 race 本身没有可靠的拉丁语来源记录。

definition_zh: 架子；置物架；使痛苦；齿条；绞尽脑汁
definition_en: a frame with shelves or bars for storing things; to cause great pain or worry; a toothed bar in a machine; to think very hard, in the phrase rack one's brains
core_image: 墙边一排木架，盘子一只只竖插在格子间
scene: 厨房的墙边立着一排木架，盘子一只只竖着插在格子里。She slid the hot tray onto the rack and stepped back.
sceneCN: 这里 rack 是「架子、置物架」（第 1 个义项：带格栅或层板用来存放物品的框架）；句意为她把滚烫的烤盘放到架子上，然后退后一步。画面里可留意：木架、竖插的盘子、冒着热气的烤盘。

pos.zh: 架子；置物架；行李架；齿条
使痛苦；折磨；绞（脑汁）

derivatives.zh: rack 加 -ing，指令人极度痛苦的，如 racking pain
rack 加 -ety，指摇摇晃晃、吵闹破旧的
rack 与 pinion 复合，指齿条与齿轮组成的传动机构

senses.title: A frame for storing things
senses.definition: a frame with shelves, bars or hooks used to hold or store objects
senses.definitionCN: 带层板、横杆或挂钩、用来放置或存放物品的框架
senses.example: Put the plates on the rack to dry.
senses.exampleCN: 把盘子放到架子上晾干。
senses.why: The noun comes from a Germanic word for something stretched out, and a frame of bars is exactly a stretched structure.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词来自一个日耳曼语词，意为被撑展开的东西，而由横杆构成的框架正是一种被撑开的结构。

senses.title: To cause great pain or worry
senses.definition: to subject someone to severe pain, strain or mental suffering
senses.definitionCN: 使某人遭受剧烈疼痛、拉扯或精神折磨
senses.example: Guilt racked him for years after the accident.
senses.exampleCN: 事故之后，负罪感折磨了他多年。
senses.why: An older meaning of the verb was to stretch a body on a frame, and from that physical stretching came the sense of extreme suffering.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词较早的意思是把人拉展在刑架上，从这种身体的拉扯生出了极度痛苦的义项。

senses.title: A toothed bar in a machine
senses.definition: a bar with teeth that engages a wheel to turn motion into a straight line
senses.definitionCN: 带齿的杆件，与齿轮啮合，把转动变成直线运动
senses.example: The steering rack turns the wheel's motion into a sideways push.
senses.exampleCN: 转向齿条把方向盘的转动变成横向的推力。
senses.why: The same frame of repeated bars appears in machinery, where a row of teeth on a bar is also called a rack.
senses.whyCN: 同一种由一排横杆构成的形象也出现在机械里，杆上排成一列的齿也被叫作 rack。

senses.title: To think very hard
senses.definition: to search one's memory with great effort, almost always in the phrase rack one's brains
senses.definitionCN: 极用力地在记忆里搜寻，几乎总用于 rack one's brains 这一说法
senses.example: I racked my brains for her name but could not find it.
senses.exampleCN: 我绞尽脑汁想她的名字，却怎么也想不起来。
senses.why: Thinking is pictured as stretching the mind on a frame, the same painful image as the older verb of torment.
senses.whyCN: 思考被想象成把心智在框架上拉展，与较早那个表示折磨的动词是同一幅痛苦的形象。

intro.en: Rack comes from Germanic words for something stretched or drawn out, and both the frame and the torment senses grew from that picture; no reliable Latin source is recorded.
intro.cn: rack 来自日耳曼语中表示「被撑开、被拉长之物」的词，架子义与折磨义都从这幅画面生长出来；没有可靠的拉丁语来源记录。

items.en: Rec meant a framework or a rack, and related verbs meant to stretch something out.
items.cn: rec 指框架或架子，相关的动词意为把某物撑展开。

items.en: Middle English rakke named a frame of bars, especially one for holding animal feed.
items.cn: 中古英语 rakke 指由横杆构成的框架，尤指盛放饲料的架子。

items.en: A related verb meant to stretch a body on a frame, which produced the sense of severe pain and torment.
items.cn: 一个相关的动词意为把人拉展在框架上，由此产生了剧痛与折磨的义项。

items.en: Machine makers used the same word for a toothed bar, because its teeth look like a row of bars.
items.cn: 机械制造者把同一个词用于带齿的杆件，因为那排齿看起来就像一排横杆。

items.en: Modern English keeps the shelf, the torment, the gear bar and the phrase about racking one's brains.
items.cn: 现代英语保留了置物架、折磨、齿条，以及「绞尽脑汁」这一说法。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words that merely resemble the spelling; the near-meaning group gathers words for shelves, frames and torment.
note.cn: 形近组收只是拼写相似的词；近义组收表示架子、框架与折磨的词。

entries.definition: A bat with strings, or a loud confusing noise.
entries.definitionCN: 带弦的球拍，或嘈杂混乱的响声。

entries.definition: Causing severe pain or strain.
entries.definitionCN: 造成剧痛或极度紧张的。

entries.definition: Noisy and rather worn out.
entries.definitionCN: 吵闹而破旧的。

entries.definition: A support fixed to a wall, or a pair of written signs.
entries.definitionCN: 固定在墙上的托架，或一对书写符号。

entries.definition: A flat board fixed to a wall or inside furniture.
entries.definitionCN: 固定在墙上或家具内部的平板。

entries.definition: A structure of bars that supports or surrounds something.
entries.definitionCN: 支撑或围住某物的杆件结构。

entries.definition: Severe lasting pain of body or mind.
entries.definitionCN: 身心上剧烈而持久的痛苦。

entries.definition: Pressure that stretches or damages something.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物被拉扯或受损的压力。

normalIntro.en: One picture holds the word together: something stretched on a frame, whether a shelf, a machine bar or a suffering body.
normalIntro.cn: 一幅画面把这个词连在一起：被撑展在框架上的东西，无论是层架、机械杆件，还是受苦的身体。

normal.en: Rack your brains is the idiom to remember: the mind is imagined as stretched on a frame until an answer appears.
normal.cn: 记住 rack your brains 这个成语：头脑被想象成在框架上拉展，直到答案出现。

normal.en: A luggage rack holds bags overhead, while a wine rack holds bottles on their sides.
normal.cn: luggage rack 在头顶放包，wine rack 让酒瓶横躺着。

normal.en: Racking pain is pain so strong it feels as if the body is being stretched.
normal.cn: racking pain 指强到像身体被拉扯的疼痛。

normal.en: A rack and pinion is a toothed bar and wheel that turn rotation into straight movement.
normal.cn: rack and pinion 是齿条与齿轮，把转动变成直线运动。

normal.en: Go to rack and ruin means to fall into complete decay, as an old frame collapsing.
normal.cn: go to rack and ruin 意为彻底败落，像一副旧框架垮掉。

abstract.en: A shelf and a torture frame share one word because both hold a body in a fixed position.
abstract.cn: 层架与刑架共用一个词，因为两者都把「身体」固定在一个位置上。

abstract.en: Racking one's brains is a small daily version of the old torment: effort applied until something gives.
abstract.cn: 绞尽脑汁是古老折磨的日常小版本：不断施力，直到某样东西松口。

abstract.en: Machines borrow human words, and a toothed bar becomes a rack because it looks like a row of shelves.
abstract.cn: 机器会借用人的词，带齿的杆件因为看起来像一排层架而成了 rack。

examples.en: He hung his coat on the rack by the door.
examples.cn: 他把外套挂在门边的架子上。

examples.en: She racked her brains for a way to explain the delay.
examples.cn: 她绞尽脑汁想找出解释延误的办法。

examples.en: The old shed had gone to rack and ruin.
examples.cn: 那座旧棚子已经彻底破败。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「瑞克」——架子一格一格像被拉开，记住 rack 是架子；想不出来就得绞尽脑汁。

root: 中古荷兰语 rec（框架）→ 中古英语 rakke（横杆框架）→ 英语 rack；同族有 racking、rackety、rack-and-pinion。没有可靠的拉丁语来源。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a stretched frame; the senses divide into a shelf, a machine bar, bodily torment and the effort of thinking.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「被撑展的框架」；义项分为层架、机械杆件、身体折磨与用力的思考。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a row of wooden frames along a kitchen wall, plates standing in the slots.
core.cn: 核心意象：厨房墙边一排木架，盘子竖插在格子里。

branches.en: a hot tray sliding into place
branches.cn: 滑进位置的滚烫烤盘

branches.en: a hand gripping a bar too long
branches.cn: 握杆太久的一只手

branches.en: teeth meeting teeth in a gear
branches.cn: 齿轮上齿与齿相咬

branches.en: a name hunted for and not found
branches.cn: 苦寻而不得的一个名字

branches.en: the same strain, once on the body and once on the mind
branches.cn: 同一种拉扯，一次在身体上，一次在头脑里

intro.en: The word is Germanic in origin and carries its meanings through a short root plus English endings for adjectives and compounds.
intro.cn: 这个词源自日耳曼语，靠一个短词根，加上构成形容词与复合词的英语词尾来承载词义。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁语同族词记录。

definition_zh: 雷达；雷达设备；洞察力
definition_en: a system that uses radio waves to detect objects and measure their position; the equipment used for this; an ability to notice things quickly
core_image: 绿色屏幕上缓慢移动的一个亮点，边缘带着淡淡的余辉
scene: 值班室里，绿色屏幕上出现一个缓慢移动的亮点，值班员记下方位和距离。The tiny blip on the radar was a fishing boat lost in the fog.
sceneCN: 这里 radar 是「雷达」（第 1 个义项：用无线电波探测物体位置的系统）；句意为雷达上那个小小的光点是一艘在雾中迷失的渔船。画面里可留意：绿色屏幕、移动的亮点、记录方位的手。

pos.zh: 雷达；雷达设备；洞察力

collocations.zh: 在雷达上；在关注范围内

derivatives.zh: radar 与 scope 复合，指雷达显示器
radar 与 man 复合，指操作雷达的人员
radar 与 dome 缩合，指保护雷达天线的罩壳

senses.title: A radio detection system
senses.definition: a system that sends out radio waves and reads the echoes to find objects and their positions
senses.definitionCN: 发出无线电波并读取回声，以发现物体及其位置的系统
senses.example: The plane appeared on radar at noon.
senses.exampleCN: 正午时分，那架飞机出现在雷达上。
senses.why: The word is an acronym built from radio detection and ranging, so the name describes exactly what the system does.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是由「无线电探测与测距」的首字母拼成的缩略词，名字正好描述了该系统所做的事。

senses.title: The equipment itself
senses.definition: the set of apparatus that produces and receives the radio waves
senses.definitionCN: 产生并接收无线电波的一整套设备
senses.example: The ship's radar failed in the fog.
senses.exampleCN: 那艘船的雷达在雾中失灵了。
senses.why: Once the system had a name, the physical set that contains it took the same name, as happens with many devices.
senses.whyCN: 这套系统有了名字之后，装着它的实体设备也叫同一个名字，许多器械都是如此。

senses.title: A knack for noticing things
senses.definition: an informal ability to sense or notice things that others miss
senses.definitionCN: 一种察觉他人忽略之事的非正式能力
senses.example: She has a radar for insincerity.
senses.exampleCN: 她对虚情假意有一种敏锐的直觉。
senses.why: A device that detects what the eye cannot see became a metaphor for a person who notices what others miss.
senses.whyCN: 一种能察觉肉眼看不见之物的人造装置，成了「能注意到他人忽略之事的人」的比喻。

intro.en: Radar is a twentieth-century acronym, not an inherited word; it was coined from the initials of radio detection and ranging.
intro.cn: radar 是二十世纪的缩略词，不是继承下来的词；它由「无线电探测与测距」的首字母拼成。

items.en: Radio waves could be bounced off objects, and the returning echo carried information about distance and direction.
items.cn: 无线电波可以从物体上反弹，返回的回声携带着距离与方向的信息。

items.en: Ranging meant measuring distance, and the time an echo takes gives the distance of the object that reflected it.
items.cn: ranging 意为测距，回声所用的时间可以给出反射它的物体的距离。

items.en: The initials of the phrase were joined into one pronounceable word during the nineteen forties.
items.cn: 这个短语的首字母在二十世纪四十年代被拼成一个可读的词。

items.en: The device was developed for detecting aircraft and ships, and the short name made it easy to say in a hurry.
items.cn: 这种装置为探测飞机与船只而发展起来，简短的名字让人在匆忙中也容易说出口。

items.en: Modern English uses radar for the device, for the technique and, figuratively, for a person's alertness.
items.cn: 现代英语用 radar 指设备、技术，也比喻一个人的警觉。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers compounds built on the acronym; the near-meaning group gathers words for detection and sensing.
note.cn: 形近组收由这个缩略词构成的复合词；近义组收表示探测与感知的词。

entries.definition: The screen that displays radar returns.
entries.definitionCN: 显示雷达回波的屏幕。

entries.definition: A person who operates radar equipment.
entries.definitionCN: 操作雷达设备的人。

entries.definition: A cover that protects a radar antenna.
entries.definitionCN: 保护雷达天线的罩壳。

entries.definition: The technology of sending signals by electromagnetic waves.
entries.definitionCN: 用电磁波传送信号的技术，radar 的前半部分即由此而来。

entries.definition: The act of discovering something that is present.
entries.definitionCN: 发现某物存在的行为。

entries.definition: Following the movement of something over time.
entries.definitionCN: 随时间追踪某物的运动。

entries.definition: A device that responds to something in its surroundings.
entries.definitionCN: 对周围事物作出反应的装置。

entries.definition: A system that detects objects under water by sound.
entries.definitionCN: 用水下声波探测物体的系统。

normalIntro.en: The name is an acronym, so its five letters carry the whole method: send radio waves, hear the echo, measure the time.
normalIntro.cn: 名字本身就是缩略词，五个字母承载了整套方法：发出无线电波、听回声、算时间。

normal.en: Radar is radio detection and ranging shortened to its initials, which is why the word has no ordinary root.
normal.cn: radar 是 radio detection and ranging 的首字母缩写，所以它没有平常意义上的词根。

normal.en: On the radar means being noticed or watched, taken from the glowing blip on a screen.
normal.cn: on the radar 指被注意或被关注，来自屏幕上发亮的光点。

normal.en: Under the radar means going unnoticed, as a plane that does not show up on the screen.
normal.cn: under the radar 指不被注意，像一架不在屏幕上显示的飞机。

normal.en: Sonar is the underwater cousin: sound navigation and ranging, built the same acronym way.
normal.cn: sonar 是它水下的亲戚：声呐导航与测距，同样用缩略法造出。

normal.en: A radar for insincerity is a metaphor: the person detects what others fail to see.
normal.cn: a radar for insincerity 是比喻：这个人能察觉别人看不见的东西。

abstract.en: Radar taught the modern world to trust what cannot be seen, as long as a machine reports it.
abstract.cn: 雷达教会现代世界去相信看不见的东西，只要有一台机器报告它。

abstract.en: The same word now names a device and a human gift, because both mean noticing what is out of sight.
abstract.cn: 同一个词现在既指装置也指人的天赋，因为两者都意味着察觉视线之外的东西。

abstract.en: Every detection system defines what counts as a signal, and that definition is a human choice inside a machine.
abstract.cn: 每一套探测系统都要界定什么算作信号，而这个界定是机器内部的人为选择。

examples.en: The storm showed up on radar two hours before it arrived.
examples.cn: 暴风雨到达前两小时就在雷达上出现了。

examples.en: The coast guard uses radar to find boats in heavy fog.
examples.cn: 海岸警卫队用雷达在浓雾中寻找船只。

examples.en: He has a radar for people who are only pretending to listen.
examples.cn: 他对那些假装在听的人有一种敏锐的直觉。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「雷打」——雷打一样的电波扫出去，碰到东西就弹回来，记住 radar 是雷达。

root: 二十世纪缩略词，由 radio detection and ranging（无线电探测与测距）的首字母拼成；没有拉丁语词源。同族有 radarscope、radarman、radome。

sensesIntro.en: The core is detection by echo; the senses divide into the system, the equipment and the figurative alertness of a person.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「靠回声探测」；义项分为系统本身、设备本身，以及比喻意义上人的警觉。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a single bright blip drifting across a green screen.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个明亮的光点在绿色屏幕上缓缓移动。

branches.en: a wave leaving an antenna and returning
branches.cn: 从天线发出又返回的一道波

branches.en: a cabinet of dials below a screen
branches.cn: 屏幕下方一排旋钮的机柜

branches.en: a host noticing a guest's false smile
branches.cn: 主人察觉到客人虚假的笑容

branches.en: the method and the box that carries it out
branches.cn: 方法与实现它的那只箱子

branches.en: the same noticing, once by a machine and once by a mind
branches.cn: 同一种察觉，一次由机器，一次由头脑

intro.en: The word is an acronym, so its parts are the initials of English technical terms rather than roots or affixes.
intro.cn: 这个词是缩略词，它的组成部分是英语技术术语的首字母，而不是词根或词缀。

latinIntro.en: No Latin source is recorded for this word, which was coined in the twentieth century.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词是二十世纪新造的，没有拉丁语来源记录。

definition_zh: 辐射；放射线；辐射热；散发
definition_en: energy that travels through space as waves or particles; the rays or particles themselves; heat transferred from a warm surface; the spreading of something outward from a centre
core_image: 一圈圈从中心向外扩散的细线，像热浪在空气里散开
scene: 实验室里，仪器旁贴着黄色警示牌，工作人员穿着厚重的防护服记录读数。The meter showed a low level of radiation near the old mine.
sceneCN: 这里 radiation 是「辐射」（第 1 个义项：以波或粒子形式在空间传播的能量）；句意为仪器显示那座旧矿附近辐射水平很低。画面里可留意：黄色警示牌、厚重的防护服、跳动的读数。

pos.zh: 辐射；放射线；辐射热；散发

derivatives.zh: radiation 的动词形式，指发出辐射、从中心向外扩散
radiate 加 -or，指散发热量的暖气片或散热器
radiate 加 -ive，指与辐射有关的
同出拉丁语「射线」一词，指半径，即从中心射出的一条线

senses.title: Energy travelling as waves or particles
senses.definition: energy that moves through space in the form of waves or particles
senses.definitionCN: 以波或粒子形式在空间中传播的能量
senses.example: The sun's radiation warms the earth.
senses.exampleCN: 太阳的辐射使地球变暖。
senses.why: Latin radiare meant to emit rays, and radiation names the whole process of energy going out in rays.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 radiare 意为发出射线，radiation 指能量以射线形式向外发出的整个过程。

senses.title: The rays or particles themselves
senses.definition: the rays or particles produced by a source, considered as things in themselves
senses.definitionCN: 由某个源产生的射线或粒子，被当作事物本身来看
senses.example: Thick walls protected the workers from radiation.
senses.exampleCN: 厚墙保护工人免受放射线伤害。
senses.why: The process and its product share one noun, so the thing that travels is also called radiation.
senses.whyCN: 过程与产物共用一个名词，于是那些传播出去的东西也被称作 radiation。

senses.title: Heat given off by a warm surface
senses.definition: heat transferred from a warm object to cooler surroundings without moving air
senses.definitionCN: 热表面在不靠空气流动的情况下向较冷环境传递的热
senses.example: The radiator warms the room by radiation as well as by hot air.
senses.exampleCN: 暖气片既靠辐射也靠热空气使房间变暖。
senses.why: Physics divides heat transfer into conduction, convection and radiation, and the third name keeps the image of rays going out.
senses.whyCN: 物理学把传热分为传导、对流与辐射，第三个名称保留了「射线外发」的形象。

senses.title: A spreading outward from a centre
senses.definition: the spreading of something, such as ideas or influence, outward from a central point
senses.definitionCN: 思想或影响等从中心点向外扩散
senses.example: The radiation of new ideas across the region took decades.
senses.exampleCN: 新思想在该地区的扩散花了几十年。
senses.why: Anything that spreads outward like rays can be described with the same noun, even when nothing physical is travelling.
senses.whyCN: 任何像射线一样向外扩散的东西都能用这个名词描述，即使传播的并非实物。

intro.en: Radiation comes from a Latin verb meaning to emit rays, built on the Latin word for a spoke or a ray, and it entered English through the language of science.
intro.cn: radiation 源自一个意为「发出射线」的拉丁语动词，其基础是拉丁语表示「辐条、射线」的词，并经科学语言进入英语。

items.en: Radius meant a spoke of a wheel or a ray of light, a straight line going out from a centre.
items.cn: radius 指车轮的辐条或一束光线，是从中心射出的一条直线。

items.en: Radiare meant to send out rays or to shine, describing light leaving a source in straight lines.
items.cn: radiare 意为发出射线或发光，描述光从光源沿直线射出。

items.en: Radiatio named the act of shining or the rays sent out, and it was used for the glow of a source.
items.cn: radiatio 指发光这一行为或发出的射线，曾用来指光源的光辉。

items.en: Scientists applied the word to energy leaving a body in waves or particles, and English adopted that use.
items.cn: 科学家把这个词用于物体以波或粒子形式放出的能量，英语接受了这一用法。

items.en: Modern English uses radiation for nuclear and solar energy, for the rays themselves, for radiant heat and for any outward spread.
items.cn: 现代英语用 radiation 指核能与太阳能、射线本身、辐射热，以及任何向外扩散。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms on the Latin stem of rays; the near-meaning group gathers words for emitted energy and outflow.
note.cn: 形近组收拉丁语「射线」词干上的形式；近义组收表示发出的能量与外流的词。

entries.definition: To send out rays, heat or a feeling.
entries.definitionCN: 发出射线、热或某种感觉。

entries.definition: A device that gives off heat into a room.
entries.definitionCN: 向房间散发热量的装置。

entries.definition: Relating to the giving off of rays.
entries.definitionCN: 与发出射线有关的。

entries.definition: A straight line from the centre to the edge of a circle.
entries.definitionCN: 从圆心到圆周的一条直线。

entries.definition: The act of sending something out.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物发送出去的行为。

entries.definition: A narrow beam of light or energy.
entries.definitionCN: 一束狭窄的光或能量。

entries.definition: The capacity to do work or to cause change.
entries.definitionCN: 做功或引起变化的能力。

entries.definition: Radioactive particles that settle after an explosion.
entries.definitionCN: 爆炸后落下的放射性颗粒。

normalIntro.en: The word is built on the image of a spoke or a ray leaving a centre, and every sense keeps that picture of something going outward.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词建立在「从中心射出的辐条或光线」这一意象上，每个义项都保留了「向外而去」的画面。

normal.en: Radiation, radius and radiate all come from the Latin word for a ray, a line leaving a centre.
normal.cn: radiation、radius 与 radiate 都出自拉丁语表示射线的词，即从中心射出的一条线。

normal.en: A radiator heats a room by giving off rays of warmth, which is why it shares the name.
normal.cn: 暖气片靠散发热射线来温暖房间，所以它共用这个名字。

normal.en: Nuclear radiation is invisible, so people measure it with counters rather than with their senses.
normal.cn: 核辐射看不见，所以人们用计数器而不是感官来测量它。

normal.en: Radiation therapy uses controlled rays to treat illness, turning the same energy into a tool.
normal.cn: 放射治疗用受控的射线治病，把同一种能量变成工具。

normal.en: The radiation of ideas is a metaphor: nothing physical travels, but influence spreads like light.
normal.cn: 思想的扩散是比喻：没有实物在旅行，但影响像光一样传播。

abstract.en: A word built from spokes reminds us that every source sends something outward, whether heat, light or fear.
abstract.cn: 一个由辐条构成的词提醒我们：每个源头都在向外发送什么，无论是热、光还是恐惧。

abstract.en: Radiation is both a danger and a cure, and the same noun names the healer and the threat.
abstract.cn: 辐射既是危险也是治疗手段，同一个名词既指救治之物，也指威胁。

abstract.en: What spreads from a centre cannot be recalled, which is why the word carries a quiet sense of consequence.
abstract.cn: 从中心扩散出去的东西收不回来，所以这个词带着一种无声的「后果」意味。

examples.en: Thin clouds do not stop all of the sun's radiation.
examples.cn: 薄云并不能挡住太阳的全部辐射。

examples.en: Workers at the plant wear badges that measure radiation.
examples.cn: 工厂的工人佩戴测量辐射的徽章。

examples.en: The radiation of the new style reached neighbouring towns within a few years.
examples.cn: 这种新风格的扩散在几年内就传到了邻近城镇。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「锐地埃申」——锐利的东西从一点向四面射出，记住 radiation 是辐射。

root: 拉丁语 radius（辐条、射线）→ radiare（发出射线）→ radiatio（发光、射线）→ 英语 radiation；同族有 radiate、radiator、radiative、radius。

sensesIntro.en: The core is rays leaving a centre; the senses divide into the energy, the rays themselves, radiant heat and any outward spreading.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「从中心射出的线」；义项分为能量、射线本身、辐射热，以及任何向外的扩散。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: fine lines spreading outward from a single point, like heat shimmering off a surface.
core.cn: 核心意象：从一个点向外散开的细线，像热浪从表面升腾。

branches.en: a sunlit stone warming in the open
branches.cn: 露天里被晒热的石头

branches.en: a badge worn to measure what cannot be seen
branches.cn: 为测量看不见之物而佩戴的徽章

branches.en: a radiator ticking as it heats a room
branches.cn: 暖气片发出轻响、温暖房间

branches.en: a style spreading from one town to the next
branches.cn: 从一座城传到下一座城的风格

branches.en: the same outward flow of heat, once from the sun and once from a pipe
branches.cn: 同一种向外的热流，一次来自太阳，一次来自管道

intro.en: The word is Latin throughout: a noun of rays, a verb of sending them out and a noun of action, with English relatives built on the same stem.
intro.cn: 这个词从头到尾都是拉丁语：表示射线的名词、表示发出射线的动词与动作名词，加上由同一词干构成的英语亲属词。

latinIntro.en: Latin radius also gave English radius, the line from the centre of a circle.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 radius 还给英语送来了 radius，即从圆心射出的一条线。
